root_cause.text: In `drivers/power/supply/pm8916_lbc.c`, the driver requested the `usb_vbus` IRQ with `devm_request_threaded_irq()` before creating/registering the `power_supply` object, so devm cleanup could free the `power_supply` before the IRQ handler was removed, letting the handler call `power_supply_changed()` on a freed or uninitialized handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `platform_get_irq_byname()` and `devm_request_threaded_irq()` from before the `power_property_read_u32_array()` / `power_supply` setup to after `devm_power_supply_register()`-related initialization, and the CVE description explicitly says the reverse devm teardown order caused a race where an interrupt could fire after the `power_supply` was freed but before IRQ unregistration, leading to use-after-free in `power_supply_changed()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove `usb_vbus` IRQ registration from the charger probe path so initialization no longer depends on that interrupt.
intent_record.what: The probe function `pm8916_lbc_charger_probe()` removes the lookup of the `usb_vbus` IRQ and the subsequent `devm_request_threaded_irq()` registration for `pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq`; the code now proceeds directly from validating the `reg` property length to reading the `reg` array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer requests or handles the `usb_vbus` interrupt during probe, so it will not receive IRQ-driven charger state change notifications through this path. This removes an interrupt dependency and may prevent probe failure due to missing or unusable IRQs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add USB VBUS IRQ handling during charger probe so charger state changes are detected via interrupt callbacks.
intent_record.what: In pm8916_lbc_charger_probe(), the code now looks up an IRQ named "usb_vbus" using platform_get_irq_byname(), returns immediately if that lookup fails, and then registers a threaded IRQ handler with devm_request_threaded_irq() using pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq as the threaded callback before continuing with extcon allocation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the charger driver will now subscribe to USB VBUS interrupt events and invoke its charger state-change handler when that IRQ fires. This enables asynchronous detection of VBUS/state changes instead of relying only on later initialization or polling, and it prevents the driver from probing successfully without a valid VBUS IRQ.

grouping_result.intent: Remove `usb_vbus` IRQ registration from the charger probe path so initialization no longer depends on that interrupt.
Add USB VBUS IRQ handling during charger probe so charger state changes are detected via interrupt callbacks.

relevance_review.reason: The change removes the usb_vbus IRQ registration from probe, directly addressing the race/order bug where the IRQ handler could run before the power_supply was safely created and managed.

The group adds USB VBUS IRQ handling in the charger probe, which matches the root cause area: requesting and using the IRQ callback around power_supply state changes. Since the vulnerability stems from the IRQ handler interacting with power_supply lifetime/order, changes introducing this IRQ handling are directly related.

candidates.rationale: This is the point where the driver acquires the USB VBUS interrupt before the power_supply object is fully set up, enabling the later IRQ handler to run while cleanup can still tear down the supply object first.
Requesting the threaded IRQ here registers the handler too early in probe, creating the lifetime ordering bug where devm cleanup may free the power_supply before the IRQ is removed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the vulnerable registration of the USB VBUS threaded IRQ before the power_supply object is fully created/registered, allowing devm cleanup ordering to free the power_supply before the IRQ handler is removed.
This acquires the usb_vbus interrupt in the affected probe path and is part of the early IRQ setup that enabled the handler to be installed before the power_supply lifetime was established.

Author: Nikita Travkin <nikita@trvn.ru>

    power: supply: Add driver for pm8916 lbc
    
    pm8916 LBC is a Linear Battery Charger hardware block in pm8916 PMIC.
    
    This block implements simple CC/CV charging for Li-Po batteries.
    The hardware has internal state machine to switch between modes and
    works mostly autonomously, only needing the limits and targets to be
    set to operate.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is present in this probe function: it requests the IRQ before registering the power_supply object. Specifically, the code does `ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq, IRQF_ONESHOT, "pm8916_lbc", chg);` and only later does `chg->charger = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &pm8916_lbc_charger_psy_desc, &psy_cfg);`. The IRQ handler calls `power_supply_changed(chg->charger);`, so if cleanup/unwind happens in the wrong order, the handler can observe an unregistered/freed power_supply handle. There is no fix in this snippet such as registering the power_supply before requesting the IRQ or otherwise deferring IRQ enablement until after the supply object exists.
